knownLimitations: The Moon's orientation is the IAU mean-Earth rotation model with its libration terms, so the Moon shows libration in longitude and latitude. It is a published series, not the JPL lunar ephemeris: its sub-Earth point and pole differ from Horizons' by at most 0.01 degrees (about 0.3 km on the surface) at the seven dates from 1969 to 2050 that were checked, and its accuracy elsewhere is not stated by the source.

A landing site placed by the IAU model (a mission reconstruction's, measured at the Sea of Tranquility) sits 0.01 km (under 0.001 degrees) from the same selenographic coordinates on this Moon at touchdown, because the reconstruction and the drawn Moon use the same IAU model (docs/ASTRAEUS_SPIKE_02.md measured 254 km, 8.4 degrees, under the earlier tidal lock).

knownLimitations: The Moon's orientation is the IAU mean-Earth rotation model with its libration terms, so the Moon shows libration in longitude and latitude. It is a published series, not the JPL lunar ephemeris: its sub-Earth point and pole differ from Horizons' by at most 0.01 degrees (about 0.3 km on the surface) at the seven dates from 1969 to 2050 that were checked, and its accuracy elsewhere is not stated by the source.

A landing site placed by the IAU model (a mission reconstruction's, measured at the Sea of Tranquility) sits 0.01 km (under 0.001 degrees) from the same selenographic coordinates on this Moon at touchdown, because the reconstruction and the drawn Moon use the same IAU model (docs/ASTRAEUS_SPIKE_02.md measured 254 km, 8.4 degrees, under the earlier tidal lock).
